[[File:Ola.gif|thumb]]
Ola was an [[initiation order]] in [[Lifeism]]. It is considered the best initiation order, and numerous systems were based on it.

It was deprecated in early 2022 in an attempt to simplify the implementation of [[also]] for easier communication.

==Historical nature==

It is based on the Asian storytelling structure of Kishōtenketsu and its application in videogame design<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dBmIkEvEBtA</ref><ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6luOrhlzvrc</ref>

[[Omega]] is Ki 起 or the introduction. It provides the simplest implementation of the rule, which helps people get comfortable with the later advances

[[Lambda]] is first represented as ''sho'' (承) with the [[Overseer]] building on the concept

[[Lambda]] is second represented as ''ten'' (転) with the [[Underseer]] adding a twist to the concept

Finally [[Alpha]] is represented as ''ketsu'' (結) with the conclusion of the concept. This can also be seen as a second appearance of the [[Overseer]]. At this point mastery is obtained of the teaching.

== Applications ==
The first introduction to Ola that [[Evolutionists]] will often encounter is the [[Covenants]] which are both organized from the [[Omega Covenant]] to the [[Lambda Covenant]] to the [[Alpha Covenant]], and the three commandments of the [[Omega Covenant]] which are structured in this form.

Most [[modules]] of [[firmlaw]] are structured this way

==Quote==
{{Quote|Starting with Omega is boring.
People who are extremely lonely or otherwise in need of compassion will do well with Omega
But Omega humbles you and helps you move up the further paths
Omega helps you be humble enough for Lambda, and then Omega helps you become a compassionate Alpha, while Lambda helps you become a competent Alpha
However you can still do wrong with starting with Omega.
Omega-Alpha order is a common phenomenon among neopagan groups, just like Alpha-Omega. Female socialization tends to make people favor Omega, while male socialization tends to make people favor Alpha. This makes people weak due to their rejection of the strength of organized religion, but generally makes them be nice people nonetheless.|[[Immanuelle Leonhart]]<ref>https://web.archive.org/web/20220726155737/https://evolution.faith/why-initiation-order-matters/</ref>}}
